title: Retrospective observational study of the functionality of dialysis access following new access creation and interventions
summary:
Background:
People whose kidneys are permanently unable to function adequately may require regular treatment to remove waste products and excess fluid from the body. For this treatment, a suitable access is needed to allow either blood (hemodialysis) or dialysate (peritoneal dialysis) to be taken from the body and returned safely and reliably. The accesses function may depend on various individual and treatment-related factors. Further procedures may be required over time to maintain or restore their function.

Research question:
The aim of this study is to investigate how long different types of access for blood-based treatments (hemodialysis) or treatment using the abdominal cavity (periotenal dialysis) function reliably and what problems may occur over time. The study will also investigate which individual characteristics, accompanying illnesses and treatment-related factors are associated with good or impaired access function. The findings will help to improve the future care of people who require kidney replacement therapy.

Methods:
The study will use information that has already been collected as part of routine patient care at the hospital. Data from adult patients who had an access for kidney replacement treatment newly created or subsequently treated will be examined. The study will assess, among other aspects, how long the access remained functional, when further procedures were required, when it could first be used reliably for treatment, and what problems occurred. Existing information about accompanying illnesses, treatments and examination results will also be considered. The study does not involve any additional examinations, treatments or contact with patients.
conditions: Diseases requiring kidney support therapy/extracorporeal therapy, as well as the function and dysfunction of dialysis access (arteriovenous fistulas, prosthetic vascular grafts, central venous dialysis catheters and peritoneal dialysis catheters, including access-related complications such as thrombosis, stenosis, infection, bleeding, primary access failure, access aneurysms, steal syndrome and heart failure).

interventions.name:
This is a retrospective, single-centre, non-interventional observational study. Only health data previously collected as part of routine clinical care will be analysed. No study-specific examinations, interventions or additional contact with patients will take place.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Creation or revision of dialysis access during the defined observation period.
- Arteriovenous fistula, prosthetic vascular graft, central venous dialysis catheter or peritoneal dialysis catheter.
- Availability of routinely collected clinical data required for the respective analysis.
Exclusion criteria:
- Insufficient documentation of data required for the respective analysis.
- Dialysis access for which the clinical course required for the respective research question cannot be assessed from the available routine clinical documentation.
